evidence_items.locator: Yusuf Mehdi's closing announcement; transcript header and technical-breakthrough discussion
evidence_items.explanation: The dated transcript records Microsoft's demonstration, restricted preview and use of a next-generation OpenAI language model. These support the timing, broad technology comparison and unfinished rollout described in the claim.

Google describes a language-model-based experimental service and says access is opening to trusted testers before wider public availability. Its testing plans support the ordinary reading of incomplete public readiness.

evidence_items.locator: Subtitle; opening paragraphs and Bard discussion
evidence_items.explanation: This contemporary report supplies the Paris event date and strongly negative reception. It distinguishes Bard's earlier advertisement error from the presentation and reports that Bard remained restricted to testing.

evidence_items.publisher: Associated Press, syndicated by Tech Xplore
evidence_items.explanation: AP documents Bard's telescope error and its own test in which Bing invented a completed Super Bowl before the game occurred. This supports similar factual-error problems while showing that contemporary coverage also criticized Bing.

An attendee explicitly favors Microsoft's demonstration over Google's initial Bard showing. His account identifies integration and user experience as reasons, so the reception difference need not imply that the underlying models differed greatly.

unresolved_gaps: No systematic media sample establishes how prevalent either reaction was.
Restricted access and factual errors establish developmental limits, but there is no objective readiness threshold in the claim.
The records do not establish equal accuracy, identical capabilities or equivalent product integration.
